title: Rotate Image
description: You are given an `n x n` matrix representing an image. Rotate it 90 degrees **clockwise**, in place: modify the given matrix directly and do not allocate another 2-D matrix. The method returns nothing.
hints: Where does the cell at row r, column c end up after a clockwise rotation? Try writing it for a 3x3 grid.
A rotation can be built from two simpler reflections of the grid.
Transpose the matrix (swap [i][j] with [j][i]), then reverse every row.

solution.explanation: A clockwise rotation equals a transpose followed by reversing each row. Transposing swaps matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for j > i, and then each row is reversed so the former first column becomes the last. Both steps touch each cell a constant number of times and need no extra matrix, so time is O(n^2) and extra space is O(1). Rotating four cells at a time layer by layer is an alternative.
